summary: A worker-placement/pickup-and-deliver hybrid where you send crew members to gather resources, then use those crew to raid settlements or complete quests for points; it plays like a streamlined descendant of Raiders of the North Sea with an added dice/animal-training layer. Turns are quick and puzzly, with a satisfying engine-build feel as your crew and animals grow more efficient over the course of the game.
praised: Smooth, low-downtime worker placement with meaningful but not overwhelming choices
Nice production and thematic art despite abstracted mechanics
Good entry point for newer gamers into worker placement/Euro design
Satisfying sense of building an efficient engine over the game
criticised: Thin theme bolted onto fairly dry mechanics — raiding and Scythian setting feel pasted on
Very similar to (and considered by some a lesser version of) Raiders of the North Sea
Limited player interaction beyond worker-placement blocking
Some randomness from dice/quest draws can feel swingy for a Euro
Can feel a bit solitaire-ish even in multiplayer

scoring.why: Points accumulate from raiding settlements, collecting plunder, and completing quests, so the winner is usually whoever balances the most scoring avenues efficiently.
